data:
Sun is a compiled language with an LLVM 20 backend.This page gives a high-level overview of the compiler. Two stages have
dedicated deep-dives:
Semantic Analysis — type inference,
scope resolution, generics, and capture detection
Code Generation — LLVM IR emission, lowering
conventions, and source layout
data.compilation-pipeline#Compilation Pipelin: Source → Lexer → Parser → AST → Manifest Processing → Merged AST → Semantic Analyzer → Borrow Checker → Codegen Visitor → LLVM IR → JIT/AOT
data.pipeline-steps#Pipeline Steps:
Lexer — Tokenize source file
Parser — Build AST from tokens
Manifest Processing — Extract manifest, parse additional source_files, load libraries
AST Merging — Combine all parsed ASTs into a single merged AST
Semantic Analysis — Type inference, scope resolution, capture detection
Borrow Checking — Ownership and lifetime analysis
Code Generation — Emit LLVM IR
JIT/AOT — Execute immediately or compile to native binary
data.component-overview#Component Overview:
Component	Files	Description	Driver	driver/driver.h/cpp	Orchestrates the full pipeline: parse → analyze → codegen → execute	CLI	cli/*.h, src/cli/*.cpp	The sun executable: command-line parsing and the fmt, test, compile, bundle and run commands	Lexer	parsing/lexer.h, parsing/nfa.h	NFA-based regex tokenizer supporting keywords, operators, literals (header-only)	Parser	parsing/parser.h/cpp	Recursive descent parser producing AST nodes	AST	ast.h, ast/*.h, src/ast/*.cpp	Expression/statement nodes with type annotations	Semantic Analyzer	semantic_analysis/semantic_analyzer.h, src/semantic_analysis/*.cpp	Type inference, scope analysis, closure capture detection	Borrow Checker	borrow_checker/*.h/cpp	Rust-style ownership and borrowing analysis (WIP)	Codegen Visitor	codegen/codegen_visitor.h, src/codegen/*.cpp	Visitor pattern for AST-to-LLVM-IR translation	LLVM Codegen	codegen/codegen.h, codegen/llvm_type_resolver.h/cpp	LLVM context, module, and type management	Compiler	driver/compiler.h	AOT compilation: emit object files, link executables	SunJIT	driver/sun_jit.h	LLVM ORC-based JIT compiler for immediate execution	Moon	moon_bundling/moon.h/cpp, moon_bundling/library_cache.h/cpp	Precompiled library format (.moon) and caching	
Headers live under include/ and implementations under src/ in the same
directory layout: support/, driver/, cli/, parsing/, ast/,
semantic_analysis/, borrow_checker/, codegen/ (with abi/ and
intrinsics/), serialization/, moon_bundling/, lsp/, debug/.
data.semantic-analysis#Semantic Analysis:
SemanticAnalyzer owns the shared context, checking helpers, and a persistent
SemanticPipeline that owns all analysis passes. Together they turn a merely parsed program into an understood one: it prepares declarations, assigns their qualified names, and registers
them before resolving signatures and analyzing bodies. The naming pass does
not resolve types or register symbols. Body analysis stamps expressions with
a resolved sun::Type. Type inference, expected-type propagation,
compatibility checking, closure capture detection, and generic
monomorphization all happen here.See Semantic Analysis for the full
deep-dive.
data.code-generation#Code Generation:
The codegen visitor walks the analyzed AST and emits LLVM IR, reading the
types and annotations the semantic analyzer recorded. Its source is split
across src/codegen/ by expression type.See Code Generation for lowering conventions and
the per-file breakdown.
data.type-system#Type System:
The type system (types.h) includes:
Primitives: i8, i16, i32, i64, u8, u16, u32, u64, f32, f64, bool, void
Arrays: Fixed-size arrays with N-dimensional indexing, owning their elements inline; ref array<T> views one with the rank erased
Functions/Lambdas: First-class function types with closure support
Pointers: ptr<T> owning pointers (RAII), raw_ptr<T> for C interop, static_ptr<T> for static data
References: ref T for borrowing without ownership transfer
Classes: User-defined value types with methods and fields
Interfaces: Contracts for polymorphism (including builtin IError; the stdlib supplies IIterator, IIterable)
Enums: Named integer variants with pattern matching support
Generics: Parameterized types with monomorphization
Errors: T throws IError functions throw classes implementing IError as native exceptions
data.jit-execution#JIT Execution:
sun program.sun
Uses LLVM ORC JIT for immediate execution without producing binaries.
data.aot-compilation#AOT Compilation:
sun -c -o program program.sun
Emits object file via LLVM, links with system C compiler to produce native executable.
data.debug-mode#Debug Mode:
sun --debug program.sun
Generates debugging artifacts in program_debug/:
ast.dot — GraphViz AST visualization
ir.ll — Full LLVM IR output
scope_tree.html — Semantic scope visualization

data:
The codegen stage walks the analyzed AST and emits LLVM IR. It relies entirely
on the types and annotations stamped by the semantic analyzer — by this point
every expression already knows its resolved sun::Type, and generic
specializations have been recorded for it to emit as ordinary non-generic code.
data.structure#Structure:
CodegenVisitor (codegen_visitor.h) walks the AST and dispatches. It does
little emitting of its own: its components do that work, each with its own
header under include/codegen/ and each owning the state it needs.They all share one CodegenState by reference — the module, the type registry,
the Sun-to-LLVM type resolver, DWARF emission, and the frame currently being
emitted. Where a component needs another, it reaches back through the visitor.
This is the same shape the semantic analyzer uses with SemanticContext.
Component	What it owns	CodegenState	The module, type registry, type resolver, DWARF, current frame	ScopeManager	The scope stack, and every drop it has to emit	FunctionRegistry	Calling conventions, where each function came from, name lookup	ClassGenerator	Classes, interfaces, generic instantiation, vtables	EnumGenerator	Enum definitions, variants, matching, payload cleanup	FunctionGenerator	Functions, lambdas, closures, returns	VariableGenerator	Variables, lvalues, globals	LoopGenerator	Loops, and the jumps out of them	ErrorGenerator	throw, try/catch, and every call that may unwind	IntrinsicsGenerator	Compiler intrinsics and libc built-ins	
Rules that need no codegen state are free functions instead, so other passes can
reach the same answers: sun::codegen::ops (support/scalar_ops.h) for scalar
widening and coercion, and sun::codegen::layout (support/struct_access.h) for
field addresses, alignment and slot writes.
data.key-conventions#Key Conventions:
LLVM is accessed through a shared context: ctx.builder and ctx.context.
Sun types map to LLVM types via the type resolver:
typeResolver.resolve(type) for variables and
typeResolver.resolveForReturn(type) for function returns.
Classes are value types: functions returning a class return the struct by
value, and callers materialize it on the stack for addressability.
A sized array array<T, N> is inline storage [N x T], carried by address
like a class, moved with a memcpy that invalidates the source. A
ref array<T> to an unsized array is the view struct
{ ptr data, i32 ndims, ptr dims } by value, built at the borrow site; its
dims table is a private constant global.
Throwing functions (T throws IError) return plain T; errors are native LLVM
exceptions (__gxx_personality_v0, landing pads), so throw unwinds and
catch selects a handler by the thrown class's type id.
Lambdas use closure structs; named functions use direct calls. Class methods
use the closure ABI: arg 0 is a ptr to { ptr func, ptr env } with the
receiver in env, and obj.method in value position is a lambda-typed bound
method { methodFn, objPtr }.
C extern globals are emitted as external-linkage LLVM globals with no
initializer. ExternCEmitter owns the resolved Sun-name to native-symbol
map used by loads, assignments, lvalues, module members, and function-pointer
calls. A sun.cabi metadata tag keeps the native name unchanged when
.moon bundling prefixes or remaps Sun symbols.
Before emitting any body, FunctionGenerator::declareBlockSignatures walks
the complete module subtree and declares every free function and class
method. Included files are one merged AST even when their declarations sit
under separate module nodes, so calls do not depend on source-list order.
Re-entering a module during emission reuses those declarations rather than
creating new ones.
Call arguments are never re-examined here. Semantic analysis records an
ArgConversion per argument on the call node, and every kind of call — plain,
module-qualified, generic, method, lambda, interface, constructor,
extern "C" — lowers its arguments through one loop, emitCallArguments, that
switches on those tags (take the address for a borrow, zero the source for a
move, build a fat pointer for an interface, extend a number, ...). Codegen
does no semantic analysis of its own.
data.source-layout#Source Layout:
include/codegen/ and src/codegen/ share one layout: a folder per component,
holding both its header and the sources that implement it.
Folder	Holds	(top level)	codegen_visitor, codegen_state, llvm_type_resolver, debug_info_builder	scopes/	The scope stack and the drop code it emits	classes/	Class and interface definitions, members, method bodies, vtables	enums/	Enum definitions, variant construction and access, matching, payload cleanup	functions/	Functions, lambdas, closures, returns, the function registry	variables/	Declarations, loads, assignments, lvalues, global initialization	expressions/	Calls, arrays and indexing, conditionals, match, blocks	loops/	for, while and for-in, and the jumps out of them	errors/	try/catch/throw and unwinding calls	support/	Helpers holding no codegen state: type checks, scalar ops, field access	abi/	The C boundary: per-target ABI classification (x86-64 SysV; AArch64 AAPCS64, ELF and Darwin variants) and the extern "C" emitter	intrinsics/	Compiler intrinsics and libc built-ins, by area, plus thread support	
Each component's *_generator.cpp holds only the forwarders it uses to reach
the rest of codegen; those cannot be inline in the headers, because the headers
are included by codegen_visitor.h.
data.adding-a-new-expression-type#Adding a Ne:
Add an ASTNodeType enum value and AST class.
Implement a codegen method on the component that owns that kind of node,
or on CodegenVisitor if it belongs to none.
Update the codegenExpression() dispatch switch to route to it.
A component that forwards sub-expression emission through its own codegen
overloads declares two forwarders,
codegen(const ExprAST&) and codegen(const BlockExprAST&). The block overload
is not optional: without it a block binds to the ExprAST one, which attaches an
expression debug location and changes the DWARF output. A deleted template
overload alongside them turns a missing overload into a compile error rather than
infinite recursion.

data: Classes define custom types with fields and methods.
data.key-features#Key Features:
Fields: Declared with var name: type; inside the class body
Constructor: init(args) { } runs during instantiation. It is written
bare — no public, no method, no return type — and so is the destructor
deinit() { }; both are always public, and no method may take their names.
A constructor that can fail is written init(args) throws IError { }.
Methods: Declared with the method keyword inside the class body; a
method can access this
Member access: Use . to access fields and call methods
Interfaces: Classes can implement one or more interfaces
Visibility: Fields and methods are private by default; mark the API public
data.field-initializers#Field Initializers:
Fields can supply values that run before the constructor body:
class Point {
    var x: i32 = 10;
    var y: i32 = this.x + 2;
    init() {}
    init(x: i32) { this.x = x; }
}
Initializers run in field declaration order on every constructor call. They
can use names from the class's definition scope, class type parameters, and
this. Constructor parameters and locals are not visible, even when they
share a name with an outer variable. Reading a field before it has been
initialized, or passing an incomplete this elsewhere, remains an error.Defaults always run, including when the constructor subsequently replaces a
field. Replacing an owning value drops the previous value normally; defaults
do not introduce implicit copies.When every field has a default and there is no constructor, Sun supplies
init(). If only some fields have defaults, write a constructor that initializes
the rest, including fields inherited from interfaces. A default that propagates
an error requires an explicit constructor with an appropriate throws
declaration; the supplied constructor is non-throwing.Field initializers also work in packed classes. Fields still require explicit
types. Struct literals must name every field and do not run these defaults.
They remain available when Sun supplies the constructor; a class with an
explicit init must still be constructed through it.
data.visibility#Visibility:
Class members are private by default; public is the only modifier.
Privacy is module-scoped: a private member is accessible from any code in the
module that defines the class (see Modules → Visibility),
and from nowhere outside it.
public module bank {
    public class Account {
        var balance: i64;                       // private
        public var owner: i32;                  // public field
        init(owner: i32) {                      // always public
            this.owner = owner; this.balance = 0;
        }
        public method deposit(n: i64) void { this.balance = this.balance + n; }
        method audit() bool { return this.balance >= 0; }   // private
    }
}
init and deinit take no visibility keyword: constructors are always
public, and deinit is invoked by the compiler and is always callable.
To restrict who can build a class, give init a parameter whose type is a
module-private class. Code outside the module cannot name that class, so it
cannot produce the argument — the standard library's SharedGuard uses this
to ensure only lock() hands out guards.
Operator methods (__index__, __setindex__, __slice__) follow the normal
rules: v[i] from outside the module needs a public __index__.
Struct literals { field: value } name fields directly, so every field
written must be accessible from the literal's location.
A method that implements a public interface member must itself be
public.
data.restrictions#Restrictions:
Because a packed field sits at an arbitrary offset, its address cannot be
handed out. Borrowing one is a compile error, the same restriction C++ places on
references to packed members:
var h: Header = Header();
ref r = h.length;   // ERROR: not aligned enough to be borrowed
takes_a_ref(h.length);  // ERROR: same reason
var len: i32 = h.length;  // OK: copy the value out
takes_a_ref(h);           // OK: the object itself is fine to borrow
Field types are restricted to what can actually be packed:
Arrays and interface values are rejected — both are multi-word fat
pointers. Use raw_ptr<T> instead.
Class-typed fields must themselves be packed_class, otherwise the
nested class's interior padding would survive and defeat the purpose.
packed_class cannot be combined with partial, which declares methods only
and so has no layout.
data.comparison#Comparison: Allocation	Syntax	Type	Memory	Cleanup	Stack	Point(...)	Point	Stack	Automatic (scope exit)	Heap (manual)	allocator.create<Point>(...)	raw_ptr<Point>	Heap	Manual (_free)	Heap (auto)	Unique<Point>(allocator.create<Point>(...))	Unique<Point>	Heap	Automatic (deinit)
data.methods-as-values#Methods as Values:
A method accessed without parentheses (obj.method) is a first-class value of lambda type: it can be stored in a variable or passed as a callback. The receiver is captured by reference, so the value carries the <'_> type marker and calls through it mutate the original object. See Bound Methods for the full rules.
var c = Counter();
var tick = c.increment;   // type: <'_>() => void
tick();                   // increments c
data.const-methods#Const Methods:
A method that does not change its object is declared const method. The
modifier sits where public does (public const method). Inside it,
this is immutable: the body cannot assign to a field, take a ref to one,
pass one to a ref parameter, or call a non-const method on this.
class Counter {
    var n: i32;
    init() { this.n = 0; }
    public const method get() i32 { return this.n; }
    public method increment() void { this.n = this.n + 1; }
}
Only const methods may be called on a constant receiver — a const variable,
a const ref, or this inside another const method:
const c = Counter();
c.get();          // ✓ OK
c.increment();    // ❌ ERROR: cannot call non-const method 'increment' on constant 'c'
A const method may still hand out a borrow of its object (method get(i) ref T,
method first() Option<ref T>). Seen through a constant receiver every
ref in the result becomes const ref — const ref T, Option<const ref T>
— so the element can be read but not changed, while a var receiver gets the
writable borrow the signature declares. Inside the method the body is checked
against that same read-only view, which is what lets it return a borrow of the
immutable this. init is never const, and a bound method value
(c.increment) follows the same rule as a call.An interface method declared const method must be implemented by a const
method; a class may mark further methods const on its own.

data: Sun provides several builtin types that are available without explicit definition.
data.numeric-literals#Numeric Literals:
Integer literals can use decimal (113), hexadecimal (0x71), or binary
(0b1110001). Hexadecimal digits accept either letter case; the prefixes
are lowercase. All bases follow the same typing and range rules, including
integer suffixes such as 0x71u16 and negative values such as -0x80i8.
Hexadecimal letters are digits, so 0xf32 is the integer 3890.Use a single _ between digits to group an integer's digits:
var entity: u32 = 0x0001_00c2;
var flags = 0b1000_0001u8;
var count = 1_000;
Separators cannot follow a prefix, precede a suffix, end a literal, or appear
consecutively. Floating-point literals do not support digit separators.An untyped integer literal is an i32 (i64 when the value needs the room),
and an untyped float literal is an f64. In a position whose type is already
known — a variable with an annotation, a field, a return — an untyped
integer literal adopts that type when its value fits.A type suffix names the literal's type directly, which is how a literal
reaches a function or constructor parameter of a narrower type. Every numeric
type is a suffix: i8 through i64, u8 through u64 on integer literals,
and f32/f64 on float literals.
var sa = SockAddrIn(0u32, 7400u16);   // without suffixes, each argument
                                      // would need a typed variable
var flag: u8 = 128u8;
var offset = -128i8;                  // the minus folds into the literal
var ratio = 1.5f32;
A value that does not fit its suffix is a compile error, not a silent wrap:
var b = 300u8;    // Error: Integer literal 300 cannot be represented as 'u8'
A suffixed literal is an ordinary typed value from then on: it widens where
any u8 would (21u8 passes to a u16 parameter) and never narrows —
converting between typed values takes _convert or safe_convert. A char
never accepts an integer literal, suffixed or not.
data.escapes#Escapes:
Escape	Meaning	\n \t \r	Newline, tab, carriage return	\\ \' \0	Backslash, single quote, NUL	\xNN	Hex. In '…' up to \x7F; in b'…' the full \x00–\xFF	\u{...}	A scalar value by code point, 1–6 hex digits. Character literals only	
Above U+007F a byte and a scalar value stop agreeing, which is why '\xFF'
is rejected and '\u{FF}' is the way to write U+00FF.String literals ("…") and template strings also support \xNN. Each escape
consumes exactly two hex digits and inserts one byte from \x00 to \xFF,
including NUL. For example, "\x08http/1.1".length() is 9. Hex digits may
use either case; missing or invalid digits are a compile error. These escapes
insert raw bytes, so the result is not necessarily valid UTF-8.
data.arrays#Arrays:
A sized array array<T, N> owns its N elements inline, wherever it lives: a
local, a class field, a global, or an element of another array. Its size is
part of its type, so array<i32, 3> and array<i32, 5> are different types.
Multi-dimensional arrays add one size per dimension: array<f64, 2, 3>.
data.ownership#Ownership:
An array is a compound value like a class: passing it by value, assigning it
to a field or binding it to a new variable moves it, and the source may not
be used afterwards. An array whose elements own something (a class with a
deinit) drops each element when the array is dropped. An element of such an
array is borrowed in place with ref or const ref; it cannot be moved out.
var a: array<i32, 3> = [1, 2, 3];
var b = a;        // a moves into b
// a[0]           // ERROR: use of moved variable 'a'
data.pointer-types#Pointer Types: Sun provides pointer types for working with memory:
data.reference-types#Reference Types:
A reference borrows a value instead of owning it. Sun never implicitly copies a
class, payload enum or interface, so a reference is how one of those is read or
modified in place — as a parameter, a local, or a return type.
data.const-ref-t---shared-borrow#const ref T:
Read-only access. Several const refs to one value may be alive at once, and a
mutable ref cannot coexist with any of them. Through a const ref nothing can
be assigned and only const methods can be called.
function total(v: const ref Vec<i32>) i64 {
    return v.size();     // ✓ size() is a const method
    // v.push(1);        // ❌ ERROR: cannot call non-const method 'push'
}
const always leads: it is const ref T, never ref const T. A ref T may be
passed or rebound as const ref T, never the other way round.
A reference is a borrow, not a pointer: it always names live storage, it
cannot be null, and it cannot be stored past the lifetime of what it borrows.
Where a by-value T is expected and T is compound, a ref T is rejected —
reading the value out of the borrow would leave two owners of one buffer.
Memory Safety has the full rules.
data.builtin-interfaces#Builtin Interfaces: Sun provides builtin interfaces for common patterns. These interfaces are always available and cannot be redefined.
data.iteration-interfaces#Iteration interface:
IIterator<T, Container> and IIterable<T, Self> are ordinary stdlib
interfaces (stdlib/iterator.sun), not builtins, because their contract names
Option<T>. See Iteration
in the standard library reference and the for-in loop.

data:
The semantic analyzer's job is to turn a merely parsed program into an
understood one: every expression gets a resolved type, every name gets a
meaning, and anything inconsistent is rejected with an error. It prepares
declarations and annotates the AST in place; the borrow checker and codegen
read those annotations.
data.semantic-analyzer#Semantic Analyzer:
SemanticAnalyzer owns the shared SemanticContext, checking helpers, and
SemanticPipeline. The context holds scopes, symbols, class shapes, and pending
extensions; the shared type registry owns semantic types and declaration IDs.
Helpers handle type inference, calls, generics, enums, and recursive body checking.The driver invokes the pipeline to prepare declarations and check bodies in
order. Passes and helpers annotate the same AST using the shared context.
Generated generic syntax enters through SemanticPipeline::prepareGenerated();
nested bodies use recursive helper calls without restarting the pipeline.
data.analysis-passes#Analysis Passes: The pipeline runs the following steps in order.
data.field-initializer-preparation#Field Init:
FieldInitializerPreparationPass supplies implicit constructors and lowers field
defaults into constructor bodies. It traverses the entire AST, including local
classes, so generated declarations exist before identity assignment and naming.
It does not require resolved signatures or types.
data.declaration-identity#Declaration Identit:
DeclarationIdentityPass assigns session IDs to declarations and their binders
throughout the tree, including function bodies. Repeated runs preserve IDs, and
reopened modules share an identity. Assignment does not resolve signatures or
change source visibility and duplicate-name checks.
data.declaration-naming#Declaration Naming:
DeclarationNamingPass assigns source names and scope paths without resolving
types or registering symbols. Declaration identity assignment already recorded
the owning modules. It preserves names supplied by
imports and specializations, including aliased bundle modules. Local declarations
receive names later, when body checking reaches their resolved enclosing scope;
local variables remain unqualified.
data.declaration-collection-and-signature-res:
DeclarationCollectionPass registers types and generic templates, then resolves
class shapes and function signatures. It collects type names across the module
tree first, allowing sibling modules to refer to each other's types. Overloads
share a source qualified name and are selected using resolved parameter types;
declaration IDs distinguish the selected targets. Sun forward declarations retain
the selected definition ID and cannot replace an available definition during
body checking. Duplicate type declarations are checked by source name within
their semantic scope; reopened modules reuse that scope.C extern globals are also registered here so functions can use them before their
source declarations. Their isCExtern flag governs unsafe access, and
c_abi_types.h provides the shared C-layout checks for extern parameters and
globals.
data.body-analysis#Body Analysis:
BodyAnalyzer checks prepared statements in source order, resolving references,
inferring types, selecting overloads, and validating statements in context. It is
a recursive helper owned by SemanticAnalyzer; the pipeline starts it after
preparation and collection.Body checking names local classes and interfaces, including their methods, before
resolving method signatures. Nested blocks, functions, and lambdas are checked
through ordinary recursion. Generic templates registered during collection are not
registered again here.
data.declaration-identities#Declaration ident:
DeclarationId is a typed integer meaningful only in its owning analysis
session. An analyzed-program snapshot retains its type registry and declaration
table after the driver is released; each editor analysis creates a new session.
Declaration annotations hold the ID; a function forwards access to
its prototype so both denote the same declaration. Parameters and members also
receive IDs. Literals and other expressions that declare nothing do not.clearComputedAnalysis() drops inferred results and resolved targets while
preserving declaration identities. resetAnalysisSession() drops both while
retaining imported source keys for registration in a new session. The
subtree helpers apply those operations to child declarations and struct-backed
bindings as well. A session marker rejects accidental reuse of an annotated
tree with another declaration table. Serialization-based cloning does not copy
session IDs, so cloned declarations are registered afresh. The specializer sends
new syntax through SemanticPipeline::prepareGenerated() before resolving it;
signature helpers and body passes do not run declaration identity passes.Computed closure captures live in prototype analysis alongside the resolved
signature. Both reset operations discard their binding IDs and semantic types.
Cloning and bundle serialization preserve the written capture lists, including
ownership and const borrows, but omit computed captures. Analysis reconstructs
those records in the destination session. Retained snapshots keep their original
captures and declaration table alive independently of later driver analyses.Ordinary resolved calls and variable references carry target IDs. Direct and
module-qualified function calls and named function values use an ID-to-LLVM-function
map. Codegen binds IDs when declaring or importing functions, including forward
declarations, externs, and generic specializations. Resolved function lookup does
not fall back to symbol names. Declaration records contain no emitted symbols.
Concrete generic calls retain their selected ID and callable signature, so codegen
and return-type inference do not reconstruct specialization names.Source, specialized, builtin, and synthetic nominal types are interned by
session declaration ID. Equality compares the session and ID; class shapes and
implemented interfaces also use IDs. Specializations are interned by their
source declaration, enclosing instance, semantic type arguments, and variadic
arguments. Abstract type parameters compare their binder IDs. Names remain in
source scopes for lookup, overload selection, visibility, and duplicate checks.
Resolved generic classes, interfaces, and enums retrieve their templates from
the retained scope tree by ID, following the specialization record to its source
declaration. The same traversal handles all three kinds without another
registry. This works after local source scopes close, including type-argument
substitution and enum const views. Source-declaration retrieval checks the owning
session before using the ID. Enum expected-type matching and match patterns also
compare declarations, so a same-named enum in an inner scope cannot stand in for
the selected template. Generic enum registration checks the current scope, so
an outer declaration does not prevent an inner declaration from being registered.
Generic names remain for diagnostics, editor navigation,
and the legacy artifact representation. Class emission tracks
completed declarations by ID. Interface dispatch caches owning and borrowed
vtables together under the concrete class and interface IDs, and rejects types
from another session. The cache belongs to one codegen run; its LLVM globals are
owned by that run's module. Enum variants retain their IDs in semantic types;
specialized variants have concrete enum owners and source-variant origins.Codegen registers local and global storage under declaration IDs. Parameters,
expanded variadic arguments, references, and loop/pattern/catch bindings use the
same rule. Captures retain the selected binding ID; their environment slot is a
separate layout decision. Field access retains a selected field ID, which the
resolved class maps to its layout index. Struct initializers retain their field
selections in source order. The method frame holds the implicit receiver. LLVM
class and enum layouts are shared by their fields and packing rather than source
names, so same-named local types can have different layouts.A source block has its own semantic scope. Once that scope closes, its resolved
result type can be reused without repeating lookup of its locals. Constructor
field defaults already refer to the bindings selected before constructor
parameters became visible, so codegen does not hide and restore parameters by
name. Imported and C globals are registered before dependent bodies are emitted.PortableDeclarationKey provides the separate representation for artifact
identity: an original declaration uses a full SHA-256 bundle digest and a
bundle-local declaration number. Instances use template and structural type
keys; generated declarations use an origin, role, and structural slot. A
session table can bind each portable key to exactly one declaration ID.The canonical encoder represents each tuple with a one-byte kind tag, an
unsigned big-endian field count, and an unsigned big-endian byte length before
each field. Counts, lengths, and integer values occupy eight bytes. Original
keys, instances, enclosing-instance bindings, and generated declarations use
D, S, I, and G. Type keys use P, N, R, Q, A, F, and U;
ordered type lists use L. An absent variadic pack uses V, so it differs from
an empty L pack. Callable keys include throwing, unsafe-call, lambda, and
reference-environment flags. Lifetime spelling is deliberately erased, matching
specialization identity. Symbol encoding hashes an E tuple containing
SUN1, the key, and the emission role, and prefixes the full hexadecimal
SHA-256 digest with _SUN1_. Tests freeze the encoding independently of
protobuf, display strings, and session allocation.At an artifact boundary, the encoder converts concrete semantic types and
specialization records directly. Nominal types refer to declaration keys without
expanding recursive fields, and conversion rejects types from another session or
sources without assigned keys. Generated variadic elements retain explicit slots;
interface receiver helpers retain a generated role. Internal specialization
comparison uses exact recursive type identity, so pointer conversions cannot
merge instances with different layouts.Bundle format 4 uses a full SHA-256 digest computed before code emission. Its
input begins with sun.bundle.v1, followed by tagged, length-prefixed records.
Source fingerprints, archive name/digest pairs, and dependency digest/alias
records are sorted before hashing. Format version, target triple, debug and
optimization settings, and compiler version/revision follow. Lengths are unsigned
big-endian integers. Emitted symbols and bitcode are excluded, avoiding a circular
identity definition. Writers and imported metadata require full lowercase digest
strings. Explicit imports reject unsupported versions; directory
discovery skips them so stale build outputs do not prevent rebuilding.The driver supplies an artifact callback immediately after source identity
assignment. It assigns original keys before imported templates can be
instantiated. The bundle scope uses ordinal one; declarations and their binders
follow in source traversal order, with sibling nodes ordered by source file and
offset. Reopened modules receive one key, imported trees keep their existing
keys, and generated instances derive their keys from their original declarations.
Executable sources receive a digest of their serialized source syntax. Compiler
builtins have a fixed ABI identity independent of session allocation.Format 4 metadata carries original declaration records, portable ownership links,
and keys for nominal and module references. Import restores these records before
attaching syntax or resolving signatures, so repeated imports share session IDs.
Imported source keys survive an analysis-session reset. Ordinary AST clones
omit declaration identities while retaining written portable
references to dependencies. Qualified names remain for source lookup, visibility,
and diagnostics; they no longer identify declarations in bundle metadata.Emission derives Sun function, method, global, vtable, and interface/enum drop symbols
from portable keys and explicit roles. The program entry point and explicit C ABI
names retain their required spellings. Runtime exception tags derive from the
same portable identity. Compiled class inventories contain canonical instance
keys and exact required method symbols; the bundle writer advertises an instance
only when all its method definitions are present.
data.scope-tree#Scope Tree:
All name resolution happens against a scope tree that mirrors the
program's structure: a global scope with module, import, function, and block
scopes nested inside it. Looking up a name walks from the innermost scope
outward, also consulting using imports and, for code that came from a
.moon library, the scope of the module that defined it. Function scopes
additionally carry context the analysis needs later — whether the function
may throw, and its return type (used to infer types in return position).
data.the-deep-walk#The Deep Walk:
During the deep walk, a few things are happening at once:
Type inference — the type of every expression is computed bottom-up
(an untyped literal is an i32, a suffixed literal like 21u8 names its
own type, a call has its callee's return type, and so on).
Expected-type propagation — types also flow top-down where context
determines them: a variable's annotation shapes its initializer, a
function's return type shapes its return expressions, a parameter type
shapes its argument. This is how untyped integer literals adopt the right
width and how Option.None learns its type arguments. A suffixed literal
arrives already typed and ignores the expected type; its value is
range-checked against the suffix instead.
Overload selection — once argument types select an overloaded method,
the chosen function signature remains attached to the callee. Later result
inference uses that signature instead of looking up the method name again.
Checking — assignments, arguments, and operators are verified for
compatibility; overloads are resolved against the actual argument types;
calls to throwing functions must sit inside try or a throwing function;
enum matches must be exhaustive.
Argument conversions — once a call's signature is settled, each
argument is tagged with how it reaches its parameter (ArgConversion:
pass by value, move, borrow, class to interface, numeric widening, and so
on — include/semantic_analysis/argument_conversion.h). The rules live in
sun::conversions::classifyArgument; codegen only carries the tags out.
Capture detection — lambdas are scanned for references to outer
variables so codegen can build their closure environments.
Field initialization — each constructor is walked once more
(checkFieldInitialization, field_initialization.cpp) to enforce the
two-phase rule and to tag every this.field = value with what becomes of
the value that was there. The walk carries the fields assigned on every
path and on some path; between them a write starts a field's life, or
replaces a value, or lands somewhere the walk cannot tell, where codegen
checks the storage at run time. A method the constructor calls is walked
the same way for a summary of what it assigns and what it needs assigned
already.
data.generics#Generics:
Generics are monomorphized here, not in codegen. When analysis meets
Vec<i32> or Option<f64>, it instantiates the template with the type
arguments bound: annotations inside the template resolve against those
bindings, and the resulting concrete type (plus, for classes, a cloned and
re-analyzed copy of the method bodies) is recorded on the template's AST
node. Codegen later walks those recorded specializations and emits each one
as ordinary non-generic code.Instantiation happens lazily at the first use, but the template's body is
analyzed in the scope the template was declared in: every generic
template records its definitionScope when registered, and the instantiators
switch currentScope to it (ScopeSwitchGuard) before pushing the transient
type-parameter / class / function scopes. So a body sees exactly the names
its author could see — its module's private helpers, the module's usings,
transitive dependencies — and never the requester's locals or imports. Only
the resulting specialized type is registered back in the requesting scope
(as a lookup fast path); identity lives in the global TypeRegistry and the
specialization list on the template's AST.Type arguments are applied once, by one of two operations. Resolving a
written annotation and substituting into an existing type are separate jobs,
and each applies the bindings in scope a single time. typeAnnotationToType
starts from source syntax — ref Vec<T> as the parser produced it — and fills
in every type parameter as it walks, so what it returns is already final.
substituteTypeParameters starts from a type with no annotation behind it,
worked out somewhere earlier: a variable's recorded type, a generic method's
signature stored on its class, the type of a captured value. Applying both to
one type is not a harmless repeat. Type parameter equality uses binder IDs,
but substitution still uses the bindings in the active definition scope.
Repeating substitution in a different template's scope can select its T. IIterable names its own first parameter T, so
class Vec<T> implements IIterable<ref T, Vec<T>> puts two unrelated Ts
within reach of a single lookup.A template has a shape of its own, distinct from any specialization.
Vec<T> with T still a type parameter is what the signature
count<T>(v: ref Vec<T>) names before anything calls it. That shape is built
much like a specialization — its members are resolved, because a template body
resolves against them — but it is never recorded as one (abstractShape in
generic_specializer.cpp). Codegen lays out every specialization recorded on
a template, and a type parameter has no layout. The same reasoning exempts a
shape from checks that need a real type: a payload enum's variants go
unvalidated, since what a T may carry is only knowable once T is a type.
Recording and validation both happen when count<i32> builds Vec<i32>.
data.access-control#Access Control:
Declarations carry visibility and a declaration ID. QualifiedName contains only
scopePath and baseName; it describes source spelling, not module ownership.
DeclarationRecord::module identifies the declaring module, including for nested
classes, members, generated specializations, and imported declarations.sun::access::isAccessible accepts public items, or private items whose declaring
module is the asking module or one of its ancestors. It compares declaration IDs
and follows the module ownership chain. Top-level source items belong to the
root; imported bundle roots have distinct module IDs, so bundle-private items
remain inaccessible to importers. Import aliases change source lookup without
changing ownership. Diagnostic module paths are reconstructed from declaration
records instead of copied from qualified names.Enforcement lives in two places:
Module-level items are filtered inside the scope lookups
(AccessFilter in semantic_scope.h, used by lookupInChain,
lookupFunction, resolveNameWithUsings, findSymbolInModule, ...). The
analyzer implements AccessContext, which tells lookups which module is
asking and reports a denial ("helper is private to module std") when
the only candidates were private.
Class / interface members are resolved on the type
(SemanticAnalyzer::accessibleField / accessibleMethod), which check the
member's visibility (owner = the type's module) where obj.member is
resolved.
Because generic bodies are analyzed inside their definition scope, "which
module is asking" is always the nearest Module scope on the stack — no
override is needed. deinit is always public (methodVisibility). Wording
of every diagnostic comes from sun::access::denialMessage
(access_checker.h).
data.source-layout#Source Layout:
The analyzer's source is split by concern under src/semantic_analysis/:
File	Responsibility	semantic_pipeline.cpp	Owning and ordering all passes within the analyzer	field_initializer_preparation_pass.cpp	Preparing field defaults and implicit constructors	declaration_naming_pass.cpp	Program naming traversal and individual local declaration names	declaration_collection_pass.cpp	Registering declarations and resolving signatures	body_analyzer.cpp	Recursive statement checking and function scopes	analysis.cpp, analysis_*.cpp	Shared expression and construct checking helpers	type_inferer.cpp	Bottom-up typing	type_annotations.cpp	Resolving written annotations, and substituting into a resolved type	semantic_context.cpp / scope_lookup.cpp	Shared scopes, symbols, and declaration bookkeeping (declaration_state.h)	generic_specializer.cpp, generic_type_arguments.cpp	Monomorphization, and inferring type arguments at a call	interfaces.cpp, enums.cpp, packed_classes.cpp	Per-construct analysis	argument_conversion.cpp, type_rules.cpp	How an argument reaches its parameter, and what is assignable to what	access_checker.cpp	Visibility	captures.cpp	Closure captures	field_initialization.cpp	The two-phase constructor rule, and what each field write drops	
Overload tables use the source name and exact structural parameter types. Nominal
parameter types compare declaration IDs, so identical spellings in different
scopes remain distinct. Generic instances retain their source qualified names;
SpecializationKey and declaration IDs distinguish their concrete arguments.
Module variables are indexed by source name within their owning scope. Encoded
portable declaration keys are used only where emitted symbols need stable names
across compilation sessions.

class sun::ast::StructLiteralAST : public sun::ast::ExprAST
Struct literal: { color: "red", speed: 120 }.Constructs a class by naming each field, for classes that declare no init. Positional construction is deliberately not offered for these: field order is a layout detail, and a positional call would silently change meaning if two same-typed fields were ever reordered.A literal carries no type of its own — it takes the type of the context it appears in (var car: Car = { ... }), which semantic analysis supplies.

class sun::borrow_checker::BorrowState
Tracks the borrow state of all variables during analysis Enforces Rust-style borrow rules:
At any given time, either ONE mutable borrow OR any number of shared borrows
Cannot mutate a variable while it has active borrows (unless through the borrow)
Borrows are invalidated when they go out of scope

class sun::borrow_checker::Lifetime
Represents the lifetime of a reference - how long it remains valid.Lifetimes form a partial order based on scope containment.Key invariants:
Static lifetime outlives everything
Param lifetimes outlive the function body (caller's scope)
Local lifetimes are bounded by their declaring scope
A reference's lifetime must not exceed its target's lifetime

class sun::codegen::LLVMTypeResolver
LLVMTypeResolver converts sun::semantic_analysis::Type to llvm::Type with proper handling of:
Primitive types (i32 -> i32, f64 -> double, etc.)
Function types -> closure struct { ptr, ptr }
Function and lambda types
It maintains a shared closure type to ensure type equality across the module.

data.codegenspawnintrinsic#codegenSpawnIntrin:
public · function · Source
Value * sun::codegen::intrinsics::IntrinsicsGenerator::codegenSpawnIntrinsic(const TypePtr &lambdaSunType, const TypePtr &contextPtrType, const std::vector< std::unique_ptr< ExprAST > > &args, const std::vector< sun::semantic_analysis::ArgConversion > &conversions)
Generates IR for _spawn<F>(fn, args...).param
contextPtrType: Pointer type of the shared thread context.
Builds the thread context on the heap — it must outlive this frame — moves the arguments into an argument block beside it, and starts the thread on a trampoline built for this lambda's signature. Hands back the context pointer; stdlib spawn wraps that in the Thread<T> handle that owns it, so the thread is joined when that handle is dropped.param
lambdaSunType: The lambda type F was inferred as.
args: The lambda followed by the arguments to move into the thread.
conversions: One ArgConversion per entry of args.
return: The thread context pointer.Related: TypePtr, ExprAST, sun::semantic_analysis::ArgConversion, ArgConversion

data.codegenthreadjoinintrinsic#codegenThread:
public · function · Source
Value * sun::codegen::intrinsics::IntrinsicsGenerator::codegenThreadJoinIntrinsic(const TypePtr &resultType, const std::vector< std::unique_ptr< ExprAST > > &args, bool dropResult)
Generates IR for _thread_join<T>(ctx) and _thread_join_drop<T>(ctx).Blocks until the thread has exited, then releases its context. Reading the result out of the slot is a move: the caller takes over whatever it owns. With dropResult nobody is taking it, so what the slot holds is dropped in place first — freeing the slot alone would release the result's own bytes and nothing they point at.param
resultType: Sun type of the thread's result (T in Thread<T>).
args: The thread context, as a single argument.
dropResult: Drop the result rather than hand it back.
return: The thread's result, or a non-null placeholder for void.Related: TypePtr, ExprAST

class sun::moon_bundling::MoonCache
Download cache for .moon bundles referenced by URL in a manifest:manifest { libraries: [{ url: "https://example.com/lib.moon" }] }Bundles are downloaded once with the system curl binary and stored under the cache directory, keyed by the URL. A cached bundle is reused forever, unless the manifest entry carries a hash (lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file bytes) that the cached file no longer matches — then it is fetched again and the fresh download must match the hash.

class sun::parsing::DFA
Lazily determinized NFA (subset construction with a transition cache)A DFA state is a set of NFA states. Transitions are materialized the first time they are taken and then cached, so a scan costs one array load per input byte instead of a walk over the NFA's active set. The state count is bounded by the regex, not by the input.Captures survive determinization because the NFA's capture bookkeeping only ever depended on which states are active, not on the path taken: a group's candidate start is written by any active enterGroup state and its end is committed by any active exitGroup state (both single global slots per group id). Those are properties of the state set, so they are precomputed per DFA state. This reproduces the NFA's semantics exactly, including its "last writer wins per group id" approximation. Path-accurate captures would need a tagged DFA with per-transition register copies; that is not built here.The Lexer bypasses captures entirely and uses acceptKind()/step() directly.

class sun::semantic_analysis::ArrayType : public sun::semantic_analysis::Type
Array type: array<T, N> or array<T, M, N> for multi-dimensional.A sized array OWNS its elements inline - [N x T] wherever it lives (a local, a field, a global, an element of another array) - and moves like every other compound value. An unsized array<T> (empty dimensions) is a view of some sized array with the rank erased; it exists only behind ref and is carried as the fat struct { ptr data, i32 ndims, ptr dims }.

Record a specialization's pack element types on its cloned prototype and check them against the pack's declared type annotation._params_of<C> for a class C means C must have a matching init overload; for a lambda, that lambda's parameters must match. Any other annotation is recorded and left unchecked. Call inside the type parameter scope, so the T in _params_of<T> resolves.Related: PrototypeAST, sun::semantic_analysis::TypePtr, sun::support::Position

TypePtr sun::semantic_analysis::TypeInferer::substituteTypeParameters(sun::semantic_analysis::TypePtr type)
Replace the type parameters in a type with what they are bound to in scope, recursing through references, arrays, and generic arguments.Apply it once, and only to a type that was resolved somewhere else — a variable's recorded type, a method signature stored on a class. Applying it to what typeAnnotationToType just returned applies the same bindings twice, and a second pass is not a no-op: a type parameter reaching this function is read in whatever bindings are in scope here, which for a type carried out of another template is a different template's parameter that happens to share its name. void sun::driver::visitTests(BlockExprAST &block, std::vector< std::string > &modulePath, bool strip, std::vector< std::string > *found, bool &sawAny)
Walk the item-level statements of a merged program, recursing through module bodies.Strip mode erases every test function; collect mode makes each one public — along with every module on the way down to it — because the synthesized runner lives at root scope and could not name anything module-private. Records each test's dotted path. Runs before moon-stub injection, so only user-written modules are visited.Related: BlockExprAST

data.linkercommandfor#linkerCommandFor:
public · function · Source
std::string sun::driver::linkerCommandFor(const std::string &targetTriple, bool staticLink=false)
Pick the link driver for a target.SUN_CC overrides the choice entirely.Static links prefer a musl toolchain for the target architecture (<arch>-linux-musl-gcc, as shipped by musl.cc) when one is installed: musl is designed for static linking (glibc's static binaries still dlopen NSS modules for name lookups), is MIT-licensed (no LGPL relink obligation on the embedded binary), and produces roughly half the binary size. When no musl toolchain is present, the triple's own GCC with -static is used.A macOS target links with Apple's own cc on a Mac; from any other host there is no driver to pick — linking Mach-O needs the Apple SDK, which cannot ship with a Linux toolchain — so stop at emit-obj and link the object on a Mac.Otherwise: host builds use cc; cross builds prefer a triple-prefixed GCC (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc), falling back to clang --target=<triple>. Returns "" when no capable link driver exists on this machine.

Whether two triples name the same operating system for bundle-matching purposes.Struct layouts and ABI decisions are baked into a bundle's bitcode per OS as well as per architecture, so an aarch64-linux bundle must never stand in for an arm64 macOS target. Apple triples spell the same system several ways (darwin, macosx), which is why this is not a plain getOS() comparison; both sides are normalized first because the common three-part spelling "aarch64-linux-gnu" would otherwise parse with an unknown OS. Environment (gnu vs musl) is deliberately not compared: those layouts are compatible.

public · function · Source
void sun::semantic_analysis::checkFieldInitialization(const sun::ast::FunctionAST &constructor, const ClassType &classType, const std::vector< sun::ast::ClassMethodDecl > &methods)
Checks a constructor against Sun's two-phase rule, and decides what each write to a field does to the value that was there.Checks that constructors initialize fields before they are read.The first phase runs until every field has been assigned. The body may assign fields, and it may call the object's own methods — the walk follows the call into the method's body with the state at that point, so a method may only read fields that already have a value, and what it assigns counts towards the constructor's own obligation. A method's write always replaces and drops, whoever calls it; before a field's first value the storage is all zero, which an owning deinit treats as nothing to release. Reading an unassigned field, or handing this to anything else, is rejected: the object is not a whole value yet. The second phase begins once every field has a value, and behaves like any other method body.A constructor that can reach its end, or a return, with a field still unassigned is rejected. That field would silently be zero — the same reason a struct literal has to name every field. A write to an owning field that only some paths have assigned is rejected too: it could neither start the field's life nor drop what it replaces.Along the way each write is tagged: a write that starts a field's life drops nothing, and every other write drops what it replaces. Nothing is decided at run time.Related: sun::ast::FunctionAST, ClassType, sun::ast::ClassMethodDecl

struct sun::ast::LifetimeParameter
One lifetime parameter, as written between the angle brackets with a leading apostrophe, before any type parameters:<'a> function pick<'a>(...) <'a, T> class Pair<'a, T> { ... }A lifetime names the stack frame a <'a> lambda's environment or a ref 'a T referent lives in, so two positions in one signature can be declared to share it. struct sun::ast::VariadicParam
The trailing value pack in a parameter list, as written at the end of the parentheses: a name, and the type annotation after its colon.args... name "args", anything the call supplies args...: _params_of<T> the parameters T's init takes, or, when T is a lambda, the parameters that lambda takesThe annotation sits where an ordinary parameter's type sits, but it stands for a whole parameter list rather than one type, and the call's arguments are checked against it. It is not a constraint in the <T: _Numeric> sense: it does not narrow which types are allowed, it says where the pack's parameters come from.A pack is not a type. It stands for however many arguments the call passes, so a declaration holding one is a template: it is monomorphized once per argument tuple, and the pack's elements become ordinary positional parameters named args.0, args.1, … in that specialization.

llvm::Type * sun::codegen::abi::sysv::pieceType(const EightbyteInfo &eb, llvm::LLVMContext &ctx)
The scalar an eightbyte is coerced to.Integers take the exact width of the bytes actually occupied, so a three-byte eightbyte is i24 rather than i32 — this is what clang emits, and matching it exactly avoids relying on the callee ignoring stray high bits. Enums define a type with a fixed set of named variants.
data.defining-an-enum#Defining an Enum:
enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }
Each variant is automatically assigned an integer value starting from 0:
Red = 0
Green = 1
Blue = 2
data.payload-carrying-variants#Payload-Carryi:
Variants can carry data, turning an enum into a tagged union:
enum Shape {
    Circle(f64),          // radius
    Rect(f64, f64),       // width, height
    Empty
}
var c = Shape.Circle(2.5);
var r = Shape.Rect(3.0, 4.0);
The only way to reach a payload is a match with a destructuring pattern,
which binds each payload position to a fresh immutable local (use _ to skip
a position):
function area(s: ref Shape) f64 {
    return match s {
        Shape.Circle(r) => 3.14 * r * r,
        Shape.Rect(w, h) => w * h,
        Shape.Empty => 0.0
    };
}
Matches on enums are checked for exhaustiveness: every variant must be
covered, or a _ arm must be present. The error names the missing variants.Rules for payload enums:
They are value types with the same ownership rules as classes: pass by
ref to borrow, pass by value to move, returned by value (moved to the
caller).
== / != are not defined on them — match is the eliminator.
Payload types may be primitives, pointers, other enums, interfaces, and
classes — including classes that own heap memory (String, Vec<T>,
anything with deinit). References, arrays, and recursive payloads
(without raw_ptr indirection) are rejected.
Payload-free enums are unchanged: plain i32 values with == comparison,
usable in extern "C" signatures. Payload enums cannot cross the C
boundary yet.
data.generic-enums#Generic Enums:
Enums can take type parameters, making reusable shapes like options and
results expressible:
enum Option<T> { Some(T), None }
enum Result<T, E> { Ok(T), Err(E) }
function find(x: i32) Option<i32> {
    if (x > 0) { return Option.Some(x * 2); }  // T inferred from the argument
    return Option.None;                        // T from the return type
}
var a = Option.Some(21);           // Option<i32>, inferred
var b: Option<f64> = Option.None;  // type arguments from the annotation
Type arguments are inferred from payload arguments where possible; a bare
unit variant like Option.None takes them from the expected type (a variable
annotation, the function return type, or an assigned field), and it is an
error when no context determines them. Each specialization is a distinct
type — Option<i32> and Option<f64> coexist independently — and matches
use the generic name in patterns:
match a {
    Option.Some(v) => v,
    Option.None => 0
}
Not yet supported: explicit type arguments in expression position
(Option<i32>.Some(5) — use inference or an annotation), nested patterns,
arrays or globals of payload enums, and moving a payload out of a match
binding. These are planned follow-ups.
data.trailing-commas#Trailing Commas:
Trailing commas are allowed in enum definitions:
enum Days {
    Monday,
    Tuesday,
    Wednesday,
    Thursday,
    Friday,
    Saturday,
    Sunday,
}
